items.prompt: The company ___ three new branches since January.

explanation.en: Since January describes a period that continues up to now, so the present perfect is needed.
explanation.es: Since January llega hasta ahora: present perfect.

optionNotes.en: The past simple needs a finished time, and since January is not finished.
Correct: an unfinished period introduced by since.
The present continuous does not combine with since for completed actions.

items.prompt: We ___ the Prado when we were in Madrid last year.

explanation.en: Last year and when we were in Madrid fix a finished time, so the past simple is needed.

optionNotes.en: The present perfect cannot be used with a finished time such as last year.
Correct: a finished action at a finished time.
The present perfect continuous is for activities continuing up to now.

items.prompt: Have you ever ___ a speech in front of a large audience?

explanation.en: After have, use the past participle: given.

optionNotes.en: Give is the infinitive; the present perfect needs the past participle.
Gave is the past simple form, not the participle.
Correct: have + past participle.

items.prompt: I ___ to the dentist two weeks ago, but my tooth still hurts.

explanation.en: Two weeks ago is a finished time, so the past simple is needed.

optionNotes.en: Correct: ago always takes the past simple.
The present perfect cannot be used with ago.
The present perfect cannot be used with ago, even with been.

items.prompt: A: Is Tom in? B: Sorry, he's ___ to the shops. He'll be back soon.

explanation.en: He has gone means he is still away; he has been means he went and has come back.
explanation.es: Has gone: todavía no ha vuelto. Has been: fue y ya ha vuelto.

optionNotes.en: Correct: he is still at the shops.
Been would mean he has already come back, which contradicts the situation.
Went is the past simple and cannot follow he's.

items.prompt: The weather ___ awful so far this summer.

explanation.en: So far this summer is a period that is not finished, so the present perfect is needed.

optionNotes.en: The past simple suggests the summer is over, but so far shows it is not.
Correct: an unfinished period with so far.
Is being describes temporary behaviour now, not a period up to now.

explanation.en: In 1965 is a finished time, so the past simple is needed.

optionNotes.en: Correct: a finished event in a stated year.
The present perfect cannot be used with a past date.
The continuous form does not fit a single finished event.

items.prompt: This is the first time I ___ sushi.

explanation.en: After This is the first time, English uses the present perfect.
explanation.es: Tras This is the first time se usa present perfect, no presente.

optionNotes.en: Correct: the fixed pattern This is the first time + present perfect.
The past simple would need It was the first time.
The present simple is a common Spanish-influenced mistake here.

items.prompt: A: Can I borrow your charger? B: Sorry, I ___ it at the office yesterday.

explanation.en: Yesterday is a finished time, so the past simple is needed.

optionNotes.en: The present perfect cannot be used with yesterday.
Correct: a finished action at a finished time.
The present continuous talks about now or the future, not yesterday.
